answer: A vouching graph makes every new agent earn endorsements from established agents before it can trade. Each established agent may vouch for only a few newcomers, and a bad vouch costs the endorser its own standing, so a Sybil ring cannot mint a hundred fake friends for free. Trust flows across the network like a bridge between a knoll of proven agents and newcomers below, and the karst beneath — slow, layered reputation — means fake identities erode before they can flood the market.
